cases.name: zero
cases.note: every axis empty, accept — the minimal signed message

cases.name: zero_reject
cases.note: every axis empty, reject — differs from accept in the final byte alone

cases.name: spec
cases.note: the reference position; the transport ids (blockID, parentID) do not appear in the message

cases.name: outer_moved
cases.note: the reference position with both transport ids changed — the message is unchanged

cases.name: degrade
cases.note: canonical slots unset: the transport ids are bound under them

cases.name: degrade_explicit
cases.note: the same position with canonical == outer stated outright — identical bytes

cases.name: max
cases.note: every field at its maximum width — catches a truncated or byte-swapped integer

layout: per vote: nodeID:20 accept:1 sigLen:4 sig:sigLen

cases.name: nova_single
cases.note: one signer at the local-execution rung — the smallest well-formed certificate

cases.name: quasar_sorted
cases.note: votes handed in descending order; the wire carries them ascending by node id

cases.name: empty_signature
cases.note: a zero-length signature — the length prefix stands alone

verdict.note: what the predicate DECIDES, not what the encoder emits. Every vote is resolved as correctly signed, so a case turns on the weighted half alone: the distinct-signer floor and the stake floor. Nova (local execution) needs signers >= novaSignerFloor(n) AND voted > floor(total/2). Quasar (export) needs voted > floor(2*total/3) and carries NO signer floor of its own. The decision does not depend on the position the votes were cast over, so a runner may weigh these votes over any position its encoder can build.

finality.name: nova_below_majority
finality.note: twenty of forty-one equal seats: exactly the majority floor, and equality is not a quorum

finality.name: nova_majority
finality.note: twenty-one of forty-one: one seat past the floor is the whole difference

finality.name: quasar_below_supermajority
finality.note: twenty-seven of forty-one: exactly the supermajority floor, refused for the same reason

finality.name: quasar_supermajority
finality.note: twenty-eight of forty-one: the export edge. Note the same twenty-eight signers clear Nova seven seats earlier — the rungs are different authorizations

finality.name: nova_one_of_four
finality.note: one of four equal seats: below the signer floor of three, refused on the count before stake is ever read

finality.name: quasar_one_of_four
finality.note: one of four equal seats at the export rung: refused on stake, which is the only floor this rung has

finality.name: nova_whale_alone
finality.note: the holder of a hundred of a hundred and four signs alone: a stake majority many times over, refused on the distinct-signer floor. Stake cannot buy a pass past the count — this is what stops a single holder self-igniting

finality.name: nova_whale_with_two
finality.note: the same holder with two of the minimum registrations: the floor is met and the same stake now carries. The floor was the binding clause, not the stake

admission.name: zero_weight
admission.note: a set carrying a validator with no stake is refused whole, never trimmed: a signer that raises the count without raising the weight is exactly the disagreement the two floors exist to prevent. The seat with no stake sorts first, so the refusal lands before any key is read. There is no admitted counterpart here: past the zero-weight clause the door asks for possession, which is the proof-of-possession vector's question and not this one

admission.name: zero_weight
admission.note: the same weight vector at the OTHER door. A set the chain already admitted is read here, not admitted here, so this door forgives what it cannot check — a key it cannot decode is skipped rather than refused. It does not forgive a key with no stake behind it. That seat is a phantom signer: it raises the count of distinct signers the Nova floor is read against and adds nothing to the stake the same certificate is weighed by, which is the disagreement between how many signed and how much signed that both floors exist to prevent. A door that admitted it would leave the floor meaning one thing at registration and another here

admission.name: weight_overflow
admission.note: two seats whose stake sums past 2^64 are refused: a total that wrapped would make every floor read off it meaningless. Checked at the already-admitted door because Register demands possession of every key BEFORE it reaches its weight clause, so that clause cannot be reached without a key ceremony

admission.name: weight_fits
admission.note: the same two seats one unit lower: the sum is representable and the set stands

weighted.note: equal stake, five validators — collapses to ⌊2n/3⌋+1
equal stake, twenty-one validators — 15, not 14: 14/21 does not strictly exceed ⅔
one validator holds most of the stake
two heavy validators cannot reach ⅔ alone
a dust registration must not move the gate
empty set — no stake model, fail closed
all weights zero — no stake model, fail closed

threshold.stakeNote: a quorum must STRICTLY EXCEED its floor. Quasar (export) needs voted > twoThirds; Nova (local execution) needs voted > half. Equality is not a quorum.
threshold.countNote: novaSignerFloor is the count guard the stake predicate cannot give — a lone holder of a stake majority must not self-ignite. equalStakeQuasar is the ⅔ count for a uniform set.

fpc.seedNote: seed = sha256(be64(epoch) || chainID || prevBlockHash). Every input is bound, and prevBlockHash is unknown until the previous epoch finalizes, so θ cannot be steered by choosing an input before the epoch opens.

seeds.note: epoch zero, no chain, no parent — every input at its floor
first epoch of a chain, genesis has no previous block
the chain moves the seed — two chains at one epoch must not share θ
the previous block moves the seed — this is what makes it unpredictable
a different previous block, everything else held
full width: a 32-byte chain id and a 32-byte parent hash
the top of the epoch range — every byte of the big-endian width is set

fpc.thetaNote: θ(phase) = θ_min + be64(sha256(seed || be64(phase))[:8])/(2^64-1) · (θ_max − θ_min), and α = ⌈θ·k⌉ is the vote count a round accepts on. thetaMin, thetaMax and theta are exact IEEE-754 bits in big-endian hex: α is a ceiling, so the last bit of θ is load-bearing.
